blind_review.assessment_recorded_from: Frozen manifest, frozen candidate and observation ledgers, canonical event/relation/route/treatment records, and exact manifest-pinned local source evidence only.

known_facts: SIM4X and SIM8X were introduced as part of the Staten Island Express Bus Redesign in August 2018.
The source says the variants were established to experiment with leveraging the Staten Island Mall Park-and-Ride.
The exact source-bound route subjects are SIM4X and SIM8X.
findings.evidence_gap_reason: The frozen evidence has exact route identities and a month, but it has no exact canonical treatment component for the route-variant/park-and-ride service design. Publishing would require inventing or substituting a treatment identity.
prohibited_inferences: Do not substitute the later Fall 2025 discontinuation-and-trip-conversion proposal for the 2018 introduction treatment.
Do not use SIM4 or SIM8 full-route service as the 2018 treatment identity.
Do not mint a route-treatment application without an exact canonical treatment component.
findings.assessment: This is an operational, route-specific event, but exact route-treatment incidence is not fully encodable from the frozen evidence; terminal insufficient_evidence is required.

known_facts: The Fare Free Bus Pilot was scheduled to begin on 2023-09-24.
The meeting minutes say selected routes were identified during the presentation, but the pinned text does not name them.
The treatment is a fare-free bus pilot.
findings.evidence_gap_reason: The exact route subject set is absent from the pinned local text, so the pilot cannot be converted into exact route-treatment incidence.
prohibited_inferences: Do not recover route names from memory, later reports, or the unavailable meeting video.
Do not infer a borough-wide or systemwide route set.
Do not publish the treatment without exact route incidence.
findings.assessment: The pilot treatment and launch date are proven, but exact route incidence is not; terminal insufficient_evidence is required.

known_facts: The source announces Queens Bus Network Redesign Phase 1 for 2025-06-29.
The adjacent source text describes network-level goals such as faster, more reliable service, an expanded frequent network, overnight service, stop changes, and new connections.
The source directs readers to an external route lookup for route-specific details.
findings.evidence_gap_reason: The frozen candidate evidence establishes the phase date and umbrella program, but it does not enumerate the exact route-treatment incidence for Phase 1.
prohibited_inferences: Do not cross every Queens route with every network-level change.
Do not import route details from an unpinned external lookup.
Do not treat a program phase date as proof that every route received every treatment.
findings.assessment: The rollout phase is operational and product-relevant, but exact route-treatment incidence is absent; terminal insufficient_evidence is required.

known_facts: OMNY Weekly Fare Capping was listed as effective 2/28 for NYC Transit in a presentation dated 2021-12-15.
The program automatically upgrades customers to unlimited rides after 12 full-fare rides in a Monday-Sunday period.
findings.assessment: This is a real systemwide fare-policy/program event applying to NYC Transit, not a bus route-treatment operational occurrence; outside_domain is the evidence-honest terminal disposition.

known_facts: The Queens Bus Network Redesign was implemented in two phases during Summer 2025.
The implementation included thousands of bus-stop signage updates, additional street changes, more than 7,000 Guide-A-Ride inserts, and a large Customer Ambassador effort.
The source characterizes the overall redesign as successfully launched.
findings.evidence_gap_reason: The retrospective umbrella account does not enumerate exact route subjects or partition the several rollout treatments by route.
prohibited_inferences: Do not cross the full Queens route network with signage, street changes, ambassadors, or rider-information treatments.
Do not substitute aggregate implementation counts for exact route incidence.
Do not publish an umbrella occurrence when exact route-treatment applications are not evidenced.
findings.assessment: The network rollout is operational and delivered, but exact route-treatment incidence is absent; terminal insufficient_evidence is required.
